styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Stone Forest, Dianchi Lake and green hills.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Rice noodles, wild mushrooms and market snacks.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Temples, ethnic villages and old streets.

stays.why: Walk to Green Lake Park, the old streets and markets. Metro nearby for trips out of town.
Handy for early trains and buses onward. Busy, plain streets; good budget rooms.
Lake views, quieter evenings and easy access to the western hills. Far from the centre.
Best for high-speed trains to other provinces. Little to see nearby; a sleep-and-go base.

food: Try Crossing-the-Bridge rice noodles (过桥米线), the city's signature bowl. Expect roughly ¥20–40.
Wild mushrooms are a summer treat. Eat them only at busy, reputable restaurants and always cooked through.
Snack streets near the old town and university area sell grilled skewers, fried potatoes and flower cakes.
Flower cakes (鲜花饼) and Pu'er tea make easy, light gifts. Buy from shops, not only tourist stalls.
Street food is cheap, often ¥5–15 a snack. Carry small cash and use WeChat or Alipay where accepted.
more_time: Add a day for the Stone Forest (Shilin): buses and trains run from the city; check times on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for a lake walk and the Western Hills near Dianchi.
Take a side trip to a nearby old town or ethnic village; ask your hostel about day tours.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the city sights and a Stone Forest day; add a night for lake and hill time.

month_notes: January: cold nights near 4°C and mild days. Pack a warm layer.
February: still cool, few rainy days. Good for walking the old streets.
March: warming up, around 22°C days. Comfortable for parks and day trips.
April: warm and mostly dry, but rain days rise. Carry a light rain jacket.
May: warm with more showers. Plan indoor sights for wet afternoons.
June: rainy season starts, about 24 rain days. Bring a raincoat and waterproof shoes.
July: wettest month, around 26 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
August: still very wet. Keep plans flexible and check the day's forecast.
September: rain eases a little but stays high. Mushroom season is at its peak.
October: cooler and drier. A good month for the lake and hills.
November: mild days, cool nights, few rain days. Great for sightseeing.
December: cool and dry with cold nights. Layer up for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Mild highland climate: cool, dry winters and a long, wet summer. Rarely hot, rarely freezing.

items.title: Best time: October to April
items.text: Mild days around 15–24°C and fewer rainy days. Ideal for parks, temples and day trips.

items.title: Wet summer (June to September)
items.text: Rain on most days, up to 26 rain days in July and August. Showers often pass; carry rain gear.

items.title: Cool nights all year
items.text: Lows drop to 4–8°C in winter. Even summer evenings are mild, so bring a light jacket.

items.title: Strong highland sun
items.text: Days are bright even in the wet season. Use sunscreen and a hat at altitude.

items.title: Mushroom season
items.text: Wild mushrooms peak in the wet months. Eat them only at busy restaurants, always cooked.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket and waterproof shoes for summer; a warm coat for winter nights.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; Didi or taxi for late nights and the airport.

modes.text: Five lines run about 07:00–22:00, fares ¥2–10. Ticket machines take paper cash only, so keep small notes.
City buses cost ¥2 and run roughly 06:00–22:00. A bus card cuts fares to about ¥0.90.
Taxis start at ¥8 plus a ¥3 fuel surcharge; insist on the meter. Didi works, and WeChat or Alipay are widely used to pay.
Not needed for city sights. Use trains and buses for day trips instead.
Fine in the centre and parks. Distances grow outside downtown, so mix walking with the metro.
Hostels rent bikes for about ¥20 a day. Shared e-bikes cost about ¥2.5 for the first 20 minutes.
Line 6 links Changshui Airport to East Bus Station, then Line 3 into downtown.
